'''Christof Geiß''' (born 1964), also called '''Geiss Hahn''' or '''Geiß Hahn''', is a German mathematician.

Geiß studied mathematics at the [[University of Bayreuth]], where he received in 1990 his [[Diplom]] with Diplomarbeit ''Darstellungsendliche Algebren und multiplikative Basen'' and in 1993 his doctorate. His doctoral thesis ''Tame distributive algebras and related topics'' was written under the supervision of Wolfgang Erich Müller and [[José Antonio de la Peña]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=66493}}</ref> Geiß does research and teaches at the [[Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México]] (UNAM), where he studied already in 1991/92 and became in 1993 an [[Academic rank#Mexico|Investigador Associado]]. He is there an [[Academic rank#Mexico|Investigador Titular C]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cristof Geiss (Investigador)|website=Instituto de Matemáticas, UNAM|url=https://www.matem.unam.mx/fsd/christof}}</ref>

His research deals with [[cluster algebra]]s in [[Lie theory]] and their categorization, pre-projective algebras, and [[quiver (mathematics)|quiver]]s in combination with [[Symmetric matrix#Symmetrizable matrix|symmetrizable]] [[Cartan matrix|Cartan matrices]].

In 2018 Geiß was an Invited Speaker with talk ''Quivers with relations for symmetrizable Cartan matrices and algebraic Lie Theory'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematics]].<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Geiß, Christof|title=Quivers with relations for symmetrizable Cartan matrices and algebraic Lie theory|year=2018|eprint=1803.11398|class=math.RT}} published in Proc. Int. Congr. of Math. 2018, Rio de Janeiro, Vol. 1, 99-124</ref>
